html:
The long war between Athens with its Delian League and Sparta with its allies.

How it went

  • 431 to 421 BCE. Sparta burned the fields of Attica each summer; Athens hid behind the Long Walls and raided by sea. The plague killed Pericles. The Peace of Nicias ended the first round.
  • 415 to 413 BCE. Athens sent a huge fleet to conquer Syracuse in Sicily and lost almost all of it.
  • 413 to 404 BCE. Sparta, now with money from the Persian Empire, built a fleet. It destroyed the Athenian fleet at Aegospotami in 405 BCE and starved Athens into surrender.

Athens lost its empire and its walls, and for a year was ruled by the Thirty Tyrants. Thucydides wrote its history as it happened.
sum: The long war between Athens with its Delian League and Sparta with its allies.
